s.note: Spiced lamb, sumac onion, yoghurt. The Turkish crime lord nobody has seen.
s.how: Brown the lamb with the onion, half the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli, then stir in the tomato paste and cook until thick. Split the dough into 4 and roll each into a long oval. Spoon the lamb down the middle, fold the sides in and pinch the ends into boat shapes, then brush the edges with egg. Bake at 230C until the crust is golden and crisp. Toss the red onion with the sumac, stir the rest of the garlic through the yoghurt, and top the pide with both and the parsley.

s.note: Golden hand-crimped beef pastries. The Argentinians had no cocaine.
s.how: Brown the beef with the onion and capsicum, add the paprika and cumin and cook until dry, then cool and fold in the egg and olives. Cut 12cm rounds from the pastry, fill each with a spoonful, fold over and crimp the edges. Brush with egg and bake at 200C until deep golden. Stir the parsley, oregano, garlic, vinegar and oil with a pinch of salt and chilli to make the chimichurri, and serve it alongside.

m.note: Paprika beef, egg noodles, sour cream. A burned Hungarian saw the devil's face.
m.how: Brown the beef in batches in the oil and set aside. Cook the onions slowly in the same pot until soft and golden, then add the garlic, paprika, caraway and tomato paste for a minute. Return the beef with the capsicum and stock, cover and simmer gently until the beef is very tender. Boil the noodles, drain and toss with the butter. Serve the goulash over the noodles with a spoon of sour cream.

m.note: Italian sausage, four cheeses and chunky tomato. Verbal's Skokie barbershop quartet.
m.how: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic, oregano and a pinch of salt until thick. Oil a deep 25cm cake tin and press the dough over the base and 4cm up the sides. Layer the mozzarella and provolone over the base, then crumble over the sausage with the fennel seeds and dot with ricotta. Spoon the tomato sauce over the top, scatter with parmesan and bake at 220C until the crust is deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into thick wedges.

w.note: Vanilla bean custard under torched sugar, cracked with a spoon.
w.how: Warm the cream with the vanilla bean until steaming, then take it off the heat. Whisk the yolks and 90g sugar until pale, then whisk in the warm cream and strain. Pour into 4 ramekins, set them in a roasting tin of hot water and bake at 150C until just set with a wobble. Chill well, then sprinkle each with sugar and torch until dark golden.
shop: 90g caster sugar, plus 4 tbsp for the tops@Pantry

d.note: Fresh espresso, vodka and coffee liqueur. Read the bottom of the coffee cup.
d.how: Shake the espresso, vodka, liqueur and syrup hard with ice in two batches. Strain into 4 chilled glasses and float 3 coffee beans on each.

shopping: 90g caster sugar, plus 4 tbsp for the tops@Pantry
